concerns.text: The 'IPhO Bench' dataset citation points to 'huggan/iphone2dslr_flower', which is an image classification dataset (cameras vs. DSLR photos), not a text-based physics Olympiad benchmark. The plan explicitly notes this mismatch but proceeds to rely on it for 'Deterministic Olympiad reasoning'. Using an image dataset for a text-generation inference pipeline renders the 'IPhO' arm of the comparative analysis impossible to execute as described. The plan must either substitute a verified text-based physics reasoning dataset (e.g., from a different verified source) or explicitly remove the IPhO component from the hypothesis test to avoid a fatal execution failure.

The 'OpenSci-Reason' dataset is cited as 'Pclanglais/open-science' (openalex_10.parquet). OpenAlex is a bibliographic database of metadata (titles, abstracts, authors) and citations, not a repository of 'ill-structured scientific problems' or 'prompts' requiring creative reasoning. Abstracts are summaries of completed work, not open-ended problems for a model to solve. Using this dataset for 'OpenSci-Reason' (generating solutions to ill-structured problems) is a modality mismatch; the data does not contain the problem statements required to test the hypothesis about 'rigid heuristics' vs. 'creative reasoning'. A dataset of actual scientific challenges or open-ended questions is required.
